On 3 December 2020 all 15 Council members approved South Africa-led draft S/2020/1158 by written vote. It became Resolution 2553. The Council reaffirmed national ownership and the country's role in setting reform assistance, with host perspectives considered in mandates. It encouraged voluntary funding aligned with national priorities, through the Peacebuilding Fund where feasible and agreed.

Germany supported voluntary reform assistance, noting the Secretary-General retains authority to manage the Peacebuilding Fund. Belgium emphasized that adequate, predictable, and sustainable funding alongside thorough coordination are essential for effective reform. While Germany focused on management authority, Belgium highlighted the necessity of specific funding characteristics and coordination mechanisms for success.

It encouraged voluntary funding aligned with national priorities, through the Peacebuilding Fund where feasible and agreed.

Germany noted penholding fell short of normal practice, allowing insufficient negotiation time. The UK, having voted yes, criticized rushed negotiations and text lacking clarity. Belgium emphasized the need for adequate, predictable, sustainable funding and thorough coordination. While Germany and the UK both addressed procedural delays and negotiation quality, Germany focused on time constraints, whereas the UK highlighted rigor and textual clarity. Belgium's position centers on financial sustainability and coordination.
